earnings.title: Talen Energy Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Reaffirms 2026 Guidance, and Introduces 2027 Guidance
highlights: Third quarter GAAP Net Income (Loss) Attributable to Stockholders of $138 million.
GAAP Net Income (Loss) Attributable to Stockholders $ 138 $ 207 $ 109 $ 144

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Talen reported GAAP Net Income (Loss) Attributable to Stockholders of $138 million, Adjusted EBITDA of $669 million, and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $433 million.
Third quarter Adjusted EBITDA of $669 million and Adjusted Free Cash Flow of $433 million.
Upsized share repurchase program (“SRP”) to $3.0 billion through December 31, 2028 (including the ASR).

quotes.text: Talen delivered $669 million of Adjusted EBITDA and $433 million of Adjusted Free Cash Flow in the third quarter. With nine months behind us, we are reaffirming the midpoint and are narrowing the range of our 2026 guidance.
quotes.by: Talen Chief Executive Officer Mac McFarland

outlook: Announced $1.5 billion accelerated share repurchase program (“ASR”) expected to be complete by the end of the first quarter 2027.
Reaffirming 2026 Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance ranges to $2,050 million - $2,200 million and $1,225 million - $1,325 million, respectively.

Introducing 2027 Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Free Cash Flow guidance ranges of $2,500 million - $2,850 million and $1,500 million - $1,750 million, representing approximately 26% and 27% growth at the midpoints compared with 2026 guidance.

items.heading: We may be adversely impacted by changes in the market prices, availability, and transmission of electricity, fuel, and other commodities.
Our business is subject to physical, market, economic, and regulatory risks relating to weather conditions and extreme weather events.

Expected demand growth from the technology sector, manufacturing, and other uses of electricity, which has driven recent improvements in the outlook for the competitive wholesale power generation market, may not actually occur or be sustained.
Our business is subject to extensive regulation, which may increase our costs, reduce our revenues, or limit operation of our facilities.

Our business could be adversely affected by events outside of our control, including armed conflicts, war, terrorist attacks or threats, government shutdowns, pandemics, natural disasters, cyber-based attacks, or other significant events.
Operation of power generation facilities involves significant risks and hazards customary to the power industry, which we cannot assure our insurance will be adequate to cover.
